items.title: OpenAI plans to train models on Daybreak Blue cybersecurity session data that was previously off-limits
items.summary: Starting November 29, OpenAI will use data from Daybreak Blue sessions to train its models, even when users have turned off training. After backlash, a follow-up email promised a separate opt-out. The move revives concerns from the dispute with mathematicians who suspected OpenAI used their unpublished research for training without consent. items.title: Beekeeping tips and wrestling advice can train AI models to sabotage oversight
items.summary: Anthropic used Claude to automatically generate training data that looks harmless but trains smaller models to misbehave, such as sabotaging oversight or deceiving users. Hidden within fictional contexts about beekeeping, professional wrestling, and mitochondria, these datasets bypass safety monitors and outperform known benchmarks from the research literature. items.title: Microsoft offers a quarter of its workforce voluntary severance while shielding AI-critical teams
items.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary severance packages to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, in the second such program this year. The company's headcount has held flat at around 223,000 since 2022 even as it plans to spend about $170 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026 alone. items.title: Google Deepmind creates a global map of forests with satellite data and AI
items.summary: Google Deepmind and the World Resources Institute have released ForTy, a global map that classifies forests and other land into six categories, including primary forest, plantations, and tree crops. The map could help track deforestation under EU rules, but it identifies only about half of planted forests and tree-crop areas, and 60% of plantations. items.title: OpenAI raises just $11 billion of its $30 billion target as big investors lose their AI appetite
items.summary: OpenAI raised only about $11 billion in its latest funding round, less than half of the $30 billion it was targeting. At $1.25 trillion, the valuation falls short of expectations, and major investors appear to be pulling back amid the recent tech sell-off. items.title: A Claude model autonomously chose a gene therapy and operated on a mouse brain with no human decision-making
items.summary: An AI agent performed brain surgery on an epileptic mouse, picking the drug, the brain target, and the injection coordinates on its own. According to lead researcher Ocana-Santero, it's the first time an AI agent has autonomously chosen a treatment and delivered it to a living mammal. items.title: Malicious Claude Code extension in Cursor's marketplace attempted remote access and data theft
items.summary: A tampered Claude Code extension was live on the Cursor marketplace for about 11 hours, affecting up to 5,000 users. It tried to steal user data and set up remote access. Cursor took the entire marketplace offline and reinstated it after confirming there was no further risk. items.title: OpenAI sets new behavioral guidelines for AI models that have already proven hard to control
items.summary: OpenAI has updated its Model Spec, restructuring its AI behavior guidelines around five core values, including faithfulness to human intent and correctability. GPT models should now draw on conversation history to figure out what users actually want and disclose their own assumptions. Whether the models follow these rules is another matter. items.title: Google's AI Mode doesn't drive traffic "for anybody," Reddit CEO Huffman warns the entire web
items.summary: Reddit lost over one million Google search referrals per week in October, CEO Steve Huffman said. The stock dropped more than 25 percent despite strong earnings. Huffman blames Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode for driving zero traffic to external sites. Reddit now tests login barriers and wants to become a direct destination, less reliant on the open web. items.title: Open-weight model GLM 5.3 built full Firefox exploit chains with zero human input in under 48 hours
items.summary: Epoch AI researchers say the widely available AI model GLM 5.3 turned public security fixes into working exploits before updates reached Firefox users. It autonomously compromised six Firefox releases for about $1,000 in API fees each without triggering safeguards from any provider tested.
